summary:
EarthPulse4 is an interactive, multisensory platform that transforms NASA's historical climate data into an engaging experience for exploring Earth's changing temperature patterns.

Using NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4), the platform allows users to explore global temperature anomalies through interactive maps, a 3D globe, historical timelines, and scientific visualizations.

Its distinctive feature is a dual-mode piano sonification system that translates global temperature trends and local geographic temperature anomalies into musical tones. This allows users to experience climate data through sound as well as visual representation.

Designed with accessibility and science communication in mind, EarthPulse4 aims to make complex climate information easier to explore and understand, including for people who are blind or visually impaired.

By combining NASA climate data, scientific visualization, interactive exploration, and mathematical sound mapping, EarthPulse4 offers a different way to connect people with the story of our changing planet.
details:
Project Details — EarthPulse4

1. Project Overview and Purpose

EarthPulse4 — Explore Earth, Hear Its Story is an interactive, multisensory climate exploration platform designed to make historical climate data easier to understand and experience.

The platform uses NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4) to explore global temperature anomalies and long-term climate patterns. It combines scientific data visualization, geographic exploration, historical analysis, and musical sonification in one digital experience.

Its main purpose is to help people connect with climate science through more than traditional charts and numerical measurements.

2. Functionality and How It Works

EarthPulse4 provides interactive tools for exploring climate data, including:

  • A 2D interactive temperature anomaly map using geographic grid data.
  • A 3D globe for exploring historical global temperature patterns.
  • Historical timelines and scientific charts.
  • Data tables for examining annual and monthly temperature records.
  • A global piano sonification experience linked to the historical timeline.
  • Real-time local piano sonification when moving the cursor over valid cells on the monthly temperature map.
  • Browser-based audio guidance and speech features.

The platform processes NASA climate datasets, organizes temperature observations by geographic location and time, and presents the information through interactive visualizations.

Missing or unavailable observations are distinguished from valid measurements to avoid presenting incomplete data as actual temperature readings.

3. Mathematical Models and Piano Sonification

A distinctive feature of EarthPulse4 is its use of mathematical frequency mapping to translate climate data into musical tones.

A. Global Timeline Piano

The global piano engine maps global temperature anomalies to equally spaced musical semitones anchored at C4 (Middle C = 261.63 Hz).

[
f=261.63\times 2^{n/12}
]

One semitone represents a 0.1°C change in temperature anomaly.

B. Real-Time Map Hover Sonification

When users activate "Listen to Earth" and move the cursor over a valid cell on the 2° × 2° monthly temperature map, the local anomaly generates an immediate musical tone.

[
f=440\times 2^{\operatorname{clamp}(x,-4,4)/4}
]

Here, (x) represents the local temperature anomaly in degrees Celsius. The audio input is limited to the range from -4°C to +4°C, producing frequencies from 220 Hz to 880 Hz.

This audio clipping does not change the original NASA values displayed on the map.

The two sound systems provide different experiences: one represents global historical changes, while the other allows users to explore local geographic variations.

4. Scientific Data Processing and Analysis

The platform uses NASA GISTEMP v4 data, including monthly and annual global temperature records and gridded NetCDF datasets.

Its processing workflow includes:

  • Reading and processing climate datasets.
  • Organizing observations by geographic grid and historical period.
  • Handling missing values and unavailable measurements.
  • Connecting geographic cells with their corresponding temperature anomalies.
  • Presenting historical trends and statistical comparisons.
  • Using latitude-weighted spatial calculations based on cos(latitude), where implemented.
  • Displaying smoothed historical trends through LOESS/LOWESS and a centered five-year moving average, where implemented.

These methods help users explore climate patterns while preserving the distinction between measured data and unavailable observations.

5. Benefits and Expected Impact

EarthPulse4 aims to:

  • Make complex climate information easier to explore and understand.
  • Support climate education and public awareness.
  • Provide an alternative auditory way to experience scientific data.
  • Improve access to climate information for people who are blind or visually impaired.
  • Help students and the public explore historical temperature changes.
  • Encourage engagement with NASA climate datasets through interactive technology.

The expected impact is to make climate science more engaging and inclusive by allowing users to explore data visually and through sound.

6. Creativity and Innovation

The main innovation of EarthPulse4 is the integration of scientific climate visualization with mathematical piano sonification.

Instead of relying only on colors, numbers, and charts, the platform translates temperature changes into musical frequencies.

Its dual-mode sonification system offers two distinct interactions: listening to global historical temperature trends through the timeline and hearing local temperature anomalies by moving the cursor across the geographic map.

Combining these capabilities with a 3D globe, historical exploration, and interactive scientific data creates a multisensory approach to understanding climate change.

7. Technologies, Programming Languages, and Development Tools

Programming Languages

  • TypeScript
  • JavaScript (ES Modules)
  • HTML5
  • CSS3

Frontend Development

  • React 19
  • React DOM
  • Tailwind CSS v4
  • Lucide React
  • Vite 8

Geographic Visualization and Graphics

  • Three.js
  • TopoJSON Client
  • World Atlas
  • HTML5 Canvas 2D
  • SVG

Backend and Data Processing

  • Node.js
  • Express.js
  • TSX
  • Vercel Serverless Functions
  • Node.js built-in modules: zlib, fs, and path

Browser Technologies

  • Web Audio API for programmatic musical tone generation.
  • Web Speech API for browser-based speech synthesis.

Accessibility Technologies

  • Semantic HTML
  • WAI-ARIA techniques
  • Keyboard navigation and screen-reader support in features implemented and tested.

AI-Assisted Development Tools

  • Google Gemini: Used as an AI-assisted tool during the user interface (UI) design process, helping explore design ideas and improve the platform's visual presentation.
  • ChatGPT: Used as an AI-powered alternative to traditional Google search to research information, explore technical concepts, understand documentation, and support the project development process.

8. Hardware and Software Requirements

EarthPulse4 is a browser-based software platform. It runs on a computer or compatible device with a modern web browser.

Speakers or headphones are recommended to experience the piano sonification and audio features.

No dedicated physical hardware is required.

9. Design Considerations

During development, the project considered several important factors:

  • Scientific Accuracy: Preserving the meaning of NASA's original temperature observations.
  • Geographic Accuracy: Correctly connecting temperature values to their geographic grid locations.
  • Temporal Consistency: Aligning historical observations with their corresponding dates.
  • Missing Data Handling: Distinguishing unavailable observations from valid measurements.
  • Audio Accuracy: Applying separate mathematical mappings for global and local sonification.
  • Accessibility: Providing an additional auditory way to explore climate information.
  • Usability: Making complex scientific information easier to navigate.
  • Responsive Design: Supporting different screen sizes and modern browsers.
  • Performance: Processing and displaying climate datasets efficiently.

10. Current Status and Future Development Plan

EarthPulse4 is structured around four main platform sections. Earth Stories Lab is currently the operational section, while the other three sections are planned for further development and activation.

The next development stage focuses on completing the remaining three sections, implementing their intended features, and connecting them with the existing platform.

Future development will also expand the scientific stories and interactive experiences, integrate additional verified environmental datasets, and improve the overall connection between geographic visualization, historical analysis, and auditory exploration.

The long-term goal is to transform EarthPulse4 into a comprehensive multisensory platform for climate education, scientific exploration, and public engagement.

11. Project Objective

EarthPulse4 aims to transform the way people interact with climate information by connecting NASA's scientific observations with interactive visualization and sound.

Its central idea is simple: climate data should not only be something people read or see; it should also be something they can explore and hear.
